notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text about Lucie’s experience of a school trip. Overall, candidates wrote concise answers, which helped them avoid grammatical inaccuracies, but some candidates did not show sufficient understanding and lifted too much of the text. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but some answers also required a minor manipulation. If candidates choose to lift more than is required to answer questions, they must make any manipulation needed in the extra material, for example replacing je with elle and changing the verb if necessary. Candidates are therefore advised to answer with the minimum number of words. For 4(a) , some candidates did not lift enough of the text, others lifted too much and invalidated their answer as they did not manipulate the extra information, e.g. la dernière journée de l’année scolaire car nous n’avons pas de cours. Some candidates did not understand 4(c) . Both parts of 4(f) required manipulation of the verbs from first to third person. Some candidates omitted a subject in both parts. For 4(i) , some candidates lifted the wrong part of the text and answered with Lucie having taken lots of photos. For 4(k) , some candidates were not selective enough in lifting the appropriate text. Their answers happened to contain the answer but did not answer the question asked. Overall, candidates answered 4(b) , 4(d) , 4(e) , 4(g) , 4(h) and 4(j) well.
notes.5: For this exercise, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from people looking for a position as an au pair. Candidates had five people and eight descriptions to choose from. Candidates had to process a variety of information and match several requirements whilst eliminating responses that did not fit. The question is aimed at the higher grades, and candidates with a wide range of vocabulary and knowledge of synonyms performed well on this section. Each person’s statement gave specific requirements for what they were looking for, such as duration, preferred location, and indicated their own specific circumstances and experience. These details excluded all answers except the correct one. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question and a global understanding of the texts will not be sufficient. For 5(a) , some candidates incorrectly chose 4 instead of 5 , but Alain only wanted to work during the summer holidays, and the position described in 4 indicated a requirement for work lasting at least six months. For 5(c) , some candidates incorrectly chose 3 instead of 1, but the advertisement indicated that the family lived in a flat in a town and Éloïse was looking for a family in the countryside. Overall, 5(b) and 5(d) were answered well. There was no pattern of incorrect answers for 5(e) .
notes.6: This final exercise about Marie and her dog Gribouille was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions could be answered with a careful lift from the text, the others needed a small manipulation of the text. Very few candidates achieved full marks, and the questions seem to have discriminated appropriately. Stronger responses were concise and straightforward, avoided adding irrelevant information and presented verb forms reasonably accurately. Weaker responses were characterised by more lengthy lifts from the text, sometimes targeting the incorrect information. For 6(a) , a selected lift was required, and many candidates answered this question successfully. For both parts of 6(b) , selected lifts were needed, but some candidates included qu’ from the text in 2 and could not be awarded the mark. Some candidates omitted the possessive in their answer to 6(c) and others targeted the wrong information in the text. Overall, 6(d) was answered well, but some added information which invalidated their answer, chose incorrect information, or did not answer this question . Some candidates successfully changed moi to elle in 6(e) , but omitted a subject and could not gain the mark. Not many candidates understood 6(f) and various incorrect answers were offered. Answers to both parts of 6(g) required a manipulation of the subject and verb from first to third person. Some candidates omitted the subject in both parts. For 6(h) , candidates often omitted the possessive and for 6(i) some candidates omitted the object pronoun le when selecting the text to answer the question.
